bounds.derivation: Let $F(z)=(\nabla_x f(z),-\nabla_y f(z))$, with strong-monotonicity modulus $\mu=\min\{\mu_x,\mu_y\}$ and Lipschitz constant at most $\beta$. Two-call extragradient with step size $1/(2\beta)$ contracts squared distance to the unique zero by at most $1-3\mu/(8\beta)$ per iteration. Starting from squared-distance bound $R^2$, iterate to tolerance $\varepsilon$ and charge both joint-gradient calls per step.

proofs.body:
Write $F(z)=(\nabla_xf(z),-\nabla_yf(z))$ and $\mu=\min\{\mu_x,\mu_y\}$. This operator is $\mu$-strongly monotone and $\beta$-Lipschitz, and its zero is the unique saddle point $z^\star$. With $\eta=1/(2\beta)$, let $w=z-\eta F(z)$ and $z^+=z-\eta F(w)$. Expanding the square, using strong monotonicity at $w$, and bounding $\|F(z)-F(w)\|$ by $\beta\|z-w\|$ gives
$$\|z^+-z^\star\|^2\le\|z-z^\star\|^2-\frac\mu\beta\|w-z^\star\|^2-\frac34\|z-w\|^2.$$
Since $\mu\le\beta$ and $\|z-z^\star\|^2\le2\|w-z^\star\|^2+2\|z-w\|^2$, the right side is at most $(1-3\mu/(8\beta))\|z-z^\star\|^2$. Starting from squared distance at most $R^2$, geometric contraction reaches the squared-distance tolerance $\varepsilon$ in $O((\beta/\mu)(1+\log(R^2/\varepsilon)))$ iterations. Every iteration uses two exact joint-gradient calls. This proof uses the full-space model of this bound.

proofs.body: Fix all public inputs and any unit vector e in the joint space. Set a_plus=z0+R e and a_minus=z0-R e, and define f_a(x,y)=(mu_x/2)||x-a_x||^2-(mu_y/2)||y-a_y||^2. Each function is uniformly mu_x-strongly convex and mu_y-strongly concave, has unique saddle a, and has joint gradient Lipschitz constant max(mu_x,mu_y)<=beta. Each saddle is exactly distance R from the public z0. With no oracle calls, any permitted deterministic algorithm has the same history and arbitrary output w on both hidden instances. The parallelogram identity gives (||w-a_plus||^2+||w-a_minus||^2)/2=||w-z0||^2+R^2>=R^2. Thus one admissible instance has squared error at least R^2, contradicting epsilon<R^2. Every successful fixed worst-case query cap is therefore at least 1. This covers arbitrary measurable computation and unqueried outputs, with no span restriction, in every admissible dimension. At epsilon=R^2 the accepted return-z0 upper bound succeeds, so the strict endpoint is sharp.

proofs.body: Use Zhang–Xu, arXiv:2609.20327v2 (2026-09-28), Algorithm 1, Assumption 3.1 and Definition 3.2 (PDF SHA256 bbeab4b027f21e83c4b21b23194d338fd92b8c7054b404a015f2711b5700f07b, pp.5–7, characters 9759–15359), and equation (6), Theorem 3.7 equations (24)–(25), Remark 3.8 (HTML SHA256 50562b606c5999850b25390aa23ee10f7757be388a7365502f34a6559222d19e, characters 16450–18250 and 37720–43920; corresponding PDF pp.12–13, characters 23700–26327). These are the unconstrained general SCSC assumptions with full-gradient Euclidean Lipschitz constant L. Set L=beta. Orient blocks so M=max(mu_x,mu_y) is the convex curvature and m=min(mu_x,mu_y) the concave curvature; when needed use g(xi,eta)=-f(eta,xi), whose complete gradient is a known permutation/sign change of one original joint-gradient response. This is an isometry and preserves the squared-distance metric. Write s=sqrt(mu_x*mu_y), choose h=2/(15 beta), rho=h M/8 and alpha=8/(8+h s), satisfying (6), and initialize v0=0 at the public z0. Theorem 3.7 gives D_T<=(32 beta^2/(m s))(1+h s/16)^(-T)D0. Set delta=epsilon/R^2 in (0,1), and T=ceil[(240 beta/s) log(32 beta^2 R^2/(m s epsilon))]. Equation (25) gives D_T<=delta D0<=epsilon; D0 itself need not be known. The algorithm uses only gradients and explicit exact-real arithmetic: query once at z0, then query the predictor and corrected point each iteration, caching the corrected joint gradient for the next predictor. Hence the fixed cap, including initialization, is 1+2T. No function values, hidden prox operators, Hessians, inner solves or certificates are supplied. If K=beta^2/(mu_x*mu_y)>=1, then 32 beta^2/(m s)<=32 K^(3/2), so this cap is O((beta/s) log(2 K R^2/epsilon)), with all logarithms displayed and universal constants. The source holds in every finite dimension, for the deterministic last iterate. For c1, retain b1 conditionally with accepted proof SIX_PROOF_395ee6ec1cc4: its squared-distance contraction factor 1-3m/(8 beta) gives the explicit cap Q_EG=2 ceil[(8 beta/(3m)) log(R^2/epsilon)]. Choose between that algorithm and PCE-DM using their public sufficient caps before making any queries. This proves the compatible upper minimum. For equal curvatures and fixed relative accuracy the new displayed branch carries an additional condition logarithm, so b1 must remain. The lower bound b5 and both upper branches have identical view, guarantee, quantity, resource and r1 domain; r2 is disjoint at epsilon=R^2. No claim is transferred from or into c3's unassessed resource projection.

proofs.body: Conditionally retain the operator premises explicitly stated in frozen /proofs/0 (SIX_PROOF_395ee6ec1cc4), canonical SHA256 ed25d4da4dc5609ff265ec3c0024b1f61acc06fe9502942c4aeee8d5bd12a394: F(z)=(grad_x f(z),-grad_y f(z)) is μ-strongly monotone, β-Lipschitz, and F(z*)=0, where μ=min{μx,μy}. These are retained premises, not a fresh recertification of the unrelated extragradient proof. The fixed contract supplies ||z0-z*||²≤R², public β and μ, complete exact gradients, deterministic adaptive algorithms, arbitrary feasible outputs, and uncharged exact-real arithmetic. Query once at z0 and output z1=z0-(μ/β²)F(z0). Writing e=z0-z*, expand: ||z1-z*||²=||e||²-2(μ/β²)<F(z0)-F(z*),e>+(μ²/β⁴)||F(z0)-F(z*)||² ≤ [1-2μ²/β²+μ²/β²]||e||²=(1-μ²/β²)||e||²≤(1-μ²/β²)R². Since 0<μ≤β, the factor is in [0,1). Thus whenever ε>0 and (1-μ²/β²)R²≤ε<R² this deterministic output satisfies the exact native squared-distance guarantee after exactly one complete joint-gradient response, including all initialization. Negating the returned dual-gradient block is known arithmetic and costs no information call. No value, Hessian, prox oracle, hidden inner solution or certificate is required. For the lower side, conditionally retain b5 at frozen /bounds/4, hash 8c2f091c42c592c0f9f463dbed24a3628fe9fe9950799751c6591553bf2b7791, and /proofs/3, hash acc1ca97d87d617054c8d4d41913e819efaebd5f8386ca4c193a68a90c272ee2. Their shifted separable quadratics remain admissible after restricting public parameters to r4, so every zero-call deterministic algorithm still fails on one instance when ε<R². Consequently N*=1 on r4. At μ=β, both block curvatures equal β and the error bound is zero, so one call exactly recovers the saddle for every positive accuracy below R². At ε=R², the unchanged return-z0 algorithm instead has exact cost zero. The r4 activation inequality is sufficient for this one-step algorithm; no converse or characterization of the largest possible one-call region is asserted. Outside r4 retain the old b1/b6 upper minimum and b5 lower side. No scientific claim is transferred to c3's unassessed resource projection.

proofs.body: Use the exact frozen native comparisons, bounds, proof records and joint ledger listed by the current curator's baseline_refs; no new external theorem is assumed. For a fixed comparison predicate and unchanged quantity, view, guarantee and resource, matching upper/lower zero implies exact complexity zero by nonnegativity. Its canonical main state is optimal and a multiplicative ratio is inapplicable. Matching positive-cost upper/lower orders likewise use optimal; saturation is a separate region property. An alias does not establish any new inequality. Aggregate summary counts are the histogram of these actual native states; missing sides are their union; only logarithmic_gap, polynomial_gap and other_quantified_gap belong to gap_classes. Joint-budget-unclosed is its own special state and does not define a scalar ratio. These are definitions of the existing Atlas status contract, not a new claim about unassessed literature. On r4, accepted b7 has actual gradient-call cost one and accepted b5 gives the integer lower bound one throughout r1 containing r4. Thus the new native c_one_call has cost exactly one under the same q1/resource. Outside that sufficient window, the retained upper/lower ratio is bounded by the displayed minimum of beta/mu and beta/sqrt(mu_x*mu_y) times accuracy logarithms; with curvature parameters varying jointly this is a registered polynomial gap, without claiming it is a mature literature-open gap or a maximal one-call characterization.
